notes: HTTP load test: ab -n 500 -c 10 against /bicycles and /bicycles/1, RAILS_ENV=production with precompiled assets (import maps + Sprockets CSS), DATABASE_URL override pointing at a local dedicated test_app_v7_to_v8_org_v6_r3_production database (its own database.yml production role/password were never provisioned locally). 0 failed requests on both endpoints. Run on port 3100, sequentially after v6 (v6's server was already stopped) -- not concurrently, unlike the earlier Ruby v3/v4 comparison, so no shared-CPU confound between the two runs.
boot_time_seconds/boot_rss_mb measured via `/usr/bin/time -l bin/rails runner "exit"` in RAILS_ENV=production, 5 samples.

test_suite duration is bundle exec rspec's own reported 'Finished in' wall time (test env, not production), 3 samples; includes SimpleCov instrumentation overhead (this app has SimpleCov configured, test_app_v6 does not) -- a real methodology difference between the two apps' suites, not just a Rails-version effect.

microbench_ips computed with the identical scripts used for v6 (iterations / Benchmark.realtime for fixed iteration counts): ar_validation 50k Bicycle#valid? calls under RAILS_ENV=production via bin/rails runner; json_roundtrip 500k JSON.generate+JSON.parse roundtrips of a representative Bicycle-shaped hash; array_sort 1k iterations of building+sorting a fresh 10k-element random Integer array -- plain `ruby`, Ruby 3.3.12. json_roundtrip and array_sort don't touch Rails/AR at all, so they're expected to land within noise of v6's numbers (and did: 1,460,920 vs 1,456,511 ips and 1,032.7 vs 1,031.6 ips) -- a useful sanity check that the harness itself isn't introducing a bias.
puma_rss_after_load_mb is RSS (ps aux, RSS column) of the single Puma worker process immediately after both ab runs completed.
